summary: Arvin crouches in the scorching shadow of a rusted fuel tanker, his grease-stained fingers trembling as he inspects a salvaged cryogenic pump. Beside him, Milo uses a jagged piece of rebar to pry open a seized valve, his face slick with sweat and desert grit. The sunlight catches the microscopic particles of dust dancing in the air between them as they work in the oppressive Mojave heat, their breathing heavy and synchronized against the backdrop of an oxidized metal graveyard.
settingText: The scorched Mojave around the mobile Launch-Shop, rocket hardware, and the converging Aegis pursuit line.

dialogueInline.text: If the seal on this pump fractures by even a millimeter, the entire combustion chamber will turn into a pipe bomb before we hit ignition.

summary: Lucia leans against the jagged edge of a solar array, her silhouette sharp against the blinding white of the salt flats as she watches Arvin. She slowly rolls a heavy, brass-cased fuse between her palms, the rhythmic clicking of metal on metal echoing in the still, dry air. Arvin stops his work and looks up, squinting into the glare, his eyes tracking the deliberate, predatory movement of her hands as she holds the critical component just out of reach.

dialogueInline.text: You spend so much time worrying about the physics of the sky that you’ve forgotten the corporate vultures are already circling the ground.

summary: Cyrus stands atop a limestone ridge, his polished Aegis tactical boots crushing a brittle desert shrub into the pale dust. He slowly raises a high-resolution optical surveyor to his eyes, the lens reflecting the distant, shimmering heat haze of Arvin’s hidden camp. His posture is rigid and military, a stark contrast to the organic chaos of the desert, and he adjusts the fit of his leather gloves with a slow, methodical pull that emphasizes his calm, predatory patience.

summary: Milo wipes a thick smear of black oil across his forehead, leaving a dark streak that emphasizes the deep lines of exhaustion on his face. He watches as Arvin meticulously aligns a series of scavenged fiber-optic cables, his hands moving with a surgical precision that Milo finds both impressive and maddening. The interior of the tanker is a cramped labyrinth of copper wiring and glowing vacuum tubes, the air thick with the smell of hot solder and recycled oxygen.

dialogueInline.text: The metal doesn't care about your blueprints, Arvin; it only cares about the heat, and right now, this hull is screaming at me.
